# Paulo Sanches

> Personal portfolio of Paulo Sanches, a Technology & Solution Architecture Manager based in Braga, Portugal, with 17+ years leading teams, solving complex technology challenges and stabilizing mission-critical programs.

The website is available in English (EN), Italian (ITA) and Brazilian Portuguese (PT), with English as the default. Mindset cards preserve Paulo’s original Portuguese and English quotes, with explanations in the selected language. Official credential names remain in English. The HTML pages are the primary sources; this file is a concise guide to their public content.

## Complete AI/Agent content

- [Complete portfolio in English (Markdown)](https://paulosanches.github.io/hello/portfolio.md)
- [Portfólio completo em português do Brasil (Markdown)](https://paulosanches.github.io/hello/pt/portfolio.md)
- [Portfolio completo in italiano (Markdown)](https://paulosanches.github.io/hello/it/portfolio.md)

These files include every portfolio section and the full text of all Field Notes. They are generated from the HTML and synchronized when the website changes. Use them for complete content; this file provides a concise discovery guide.

Each Field Note also has an individual `story.md` file and an `agent/` text view beneath its article URL, in every language. The article's Markdown alternate and AI/Agent link open that specific story. Home and story navigation within the Markdown keeps AI/Agent mode, and language switching preserves the current story.

## Profile and experience

- [Profile](https://paulosanches.github.io/hello/#profile): Business transformation through technology and AI, working with teams and AI agents from strategy to execution. Paulo manages a 60+ professional DevOps capability and provides cross-practice technical leadership to 20+ architects.
- [Experience](https://paulosanches.github.io/hello/#journey): Current projects and a condensed earlier-career summary. The current engagements include a €7M European public-sector transformation, enterprise solutioning and AWS partnerships with contributions to €3.5M in won contracts, and an active enterprise workforce and portfolio platform. Some engagements run in parallel.

## First-hand writing and mindset

- [Field Notes](https://paulosanches.github.io/hello/#stories): Experiences from Paulo’s career, written from his perspective.
- [What can you build in a weekend with a phone and AI?](https://paulosanches.github.io/hello/field-notes/a-weekend-a-phone-and-ai/): Paulo’s account of building this portfolio over a weekend by guiding Codex through text and voice from his phone. The story covers supplied career materials, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, Python locale generation, GitHub versioning and deployment, browser checks, theme interactions and free GitHub Pages hosting without Vercel or Supabase. It distinguishes mobile direction and review from code execution in the agent’s development environment. Its cover diagram shows locale generation and verification within the Codex workspace before versioning and deployment, with static language pages hosted on GitHub Pages.
- [A week at the beach. A security incident on day two.](https://paulosanches.github.io/hello/field-notes/security-at-the-beach/): A production security incident involving Liferay Portal, with lessons about maintenance and support, technical response, stakeholder communication and preparing for remote work. The incident date, client name, software version and vulnerability identifiers are not disclosed.
- [I flew to Brazil’s largest bank with a few bullet points as my brief.](https://paulosanches.github.io/hello/field-notes/banking-handover-in-brasilia/): A two-week banking handover in Brasília. Paulo listened to four stakeholders, aligned their expectations and prioritised workshops, defects and training. Client workstation restrictions and a failed PC cost him a night’s unpublished work; he resumed the fixes and addressed the client’s priorities. The bank is not named, and the visit date and technical stack are not disclosed.
- [We built a system to support families after Brumadinho.](https://paulosanches.github.io/hello/field-notes/supporting-families-after-brumadinho/): Paulo’s first-hand account of mobilising a multidisciplinary team of six after the January 2019 disaster. They built a registration and follow-up system for social workers, adapted it as requirements developed and supported it in production. The project was initially planned for two months and extended by six, totalling eight. The story credits five colleagues through the LinkedIn links he supplied and recalls the trust built on an earlier project. The client, technology stack and number of families assisted are not disclosed.
- [“Do you know Zeno Rocha?”](https://paulosanches.github.io/hello/field-notes/do-you-know-zeno-rocha/): Between 2012 and 2016, Paulo ended front-end interviews with this question, using the answer as a hiring consideration. He recounts following technical authors and community contributors, hearing Zeno speak in Recife and looking for curiosity and interest in continued learning when forming teams. The article retains the exact question in Portuguese in every language version and links to the references he followed. The uploaded event photograph serves as the cover without asserting the event name, date or identities of the people shown.
- [How did one week helping with a crisis turn into three months in São Paulo?](https://paulosanches.github.io/hello/field-notes/one-week-three-months-in-sao-paulo/): Paulo’s account of a one-week crisis assignment in April 2017 that grew into three months of work in São Paulo. His earlier automotive-finance interface work reduced review and approval time to minutes. At the telecom client, other specialists investigated a PDF billing failure while Paulo took on the marketing backlog, proposed a work plan and later organised teams for a new contract. He recounts a weekend visit home, collaboration with specialists from an acquired company and the personal cost of the extended assignment. The client is unnamed, and the billing failure’s root cause and resolution are not asserted.
- [The day I thought the company would grind to a halt because our senior developer resigned](https://paulosanches.github.io/hello/field-notes/when-our-senior-developer-resigned/): Paulo’s account of joining a global advertising agency in Recife’s Porto Digital in 2009 as the most junior ActionScript developer. After two years learning from a senior colleague, he feared that colleague’s departure would stop the team. The team reorganised and Paulo later grew into leadership. He credits Tairone César, recalls the Jurassic Park line “Life finds a way”, and ends with the supplied YouTube link to a lunch-break prank. The agency is unnamed and no departure date is asserted.
- [Mindset](https://paulosanches.github.io/hello/#mindset): Approved personal principles and their context, including preparing for setbacks, learning through pressure, planning enough to act, adapting when plans meet reality, bringing game-day energy to the team, and delivering work early to get feedback and improve it instead of waiting for perfection.

## Contributions and certifications

- [Contributions](https://paulosanches.github.io/hello/#contributions): JNation 2026 in Coimbra representing Accenture; a 2025 AI hackathon across Lisbon, Braga and Coimbra; a Cubo Tech Lead participation; and FlashCamp 2010 representing Ogilvy.
- [Certifications](https://paulosanches.github.io/hello/#certifications): Credentials and learning from Deel, Accenture, AWS, Google Cloud, Scaled Agile and Scrum Alliance. Each card includes its issuer, description and supplied dates. The section includes historical credentials with expiry dates, rather than claiming every credential is currently valid.
